about: Every fixture is a complete document. Both validators (Python here, autopilot Node later) run this list: `valid` must be accepted; `invalid` must be rejected with reject_code as the FIRST reported code and no accepted-by-accident. doc=metrics validates against schemas/qualification-feed-v2.schema.json, doc=record against schemas/qualification-record.schema.json. SCHEMA-coded rejections are expressible in JSON Schema alone; the other codes are semantic and must be reimplemented in Node. max_bytes, when present, overrides the byte cap for that case. reject_hint (SCHEMA cases) is a substring the Python validator's message must contain so a case cannot pass for the wrong reason; Node need only reject.

cases.why: production shape: one retained row per task, n_attempts and n_timeout null
population latest_per_task claiming an n_attempts (all-attempt numbers under the wrong label)
NaN is not JSON (Node's parser rejects it; Python must refuse before persisting)
duplicate object key: JSON.parse would silently keep the last, Python's json the last too, so both refuse
integer beyond +-(2^53-1): Node would round it
n_pass + n_timeout > n_attempts: a passed attempt cannot also have used up the step cap
qualification entry + two strike_events, one lifted
verbatim committed schema-1 row_digest record: legacy keeps its basis
schema-2 record whose record_id is the v1 hash of its own fields
pass_rate_permille 872.0: not the canonical JSON.stringify spelling (Node refuses the literal; Python json.dumps would write it)
cost_basis unknown with amounts 0: unknown is null, never 0
two strike_events of one seat share strike_seq 1
benchmark_observation entry also carrying a qualification block
same entry_id, different payload bytes: conflict, never merged
a valid document that exceeds the size cap (manifest max_bytes override; the default 4 MiB cap is tested separately)
